explanation: Y181C causes nevirapine resistance by eliminating a critical aromatic interaction at the core of the NNRTI pocket. The tyrosine-to-cysteine substitution removes the bulky aromatic ring while reducing overall volume by ~85 Ų, disrupting stabilizing van der Waals contacts and potentially π-π stacking or aromatic interactions that the native tyrosine maintains with nevirapine's aromatic moieties at 3.8 Å separation. The loss of the larger hydrophobic aromatic side chain creates a cavity defect in the binding pocket that destabilizes the inhibitor's accommodation, reducing binding affinity by ~1.35 kcal/mol despite retention of neutral charge at this position.
